title: Verdier trace classes commute with restriction to an open subscheme of the support
statement:
Fix the coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], $A=A_{E,n}$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $X,C$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $c=(c_1,c_2):C\to X\times_sX$ be an admissible correspondence with $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and $u:Lc_2^*K\to Rc_1^!K$ as in [def-trf-correspondence], and let $j_W:W\hookrightarrow C$ be the inclusion of an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Put $c|_W=c\circ j_W=(c_1j_W,c_2j_W):W\to X\times_sX$ and let
$$
u|_W:L(c_2j_W)^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Lj_W^*Lc_2^*K\xrightarrow{Lj_W^*u}Lj_W^*Rc_1^!K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rj_W^!Rc_1^!K\xrightarrow{\sim}R(c_1j_W)^!K,
$$
using the pullback composition isomorphism of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the identification $Lj_W^*\cong Rj_W^!$ for the open immersion $j_W$ (clause (6) of [prop-functor-package], relative dimension $0$) and the composition isomorphism of [def-trf-admissibility]. Let $F=\operatorname{Fix}(c)$ with $i_F:F\to C$ as in [def-trf-fixed-scheme], and let $j':F_W=i_F^{-1}(W)\hookrightarrow F$ be the open subscheme over $W$; the fibre-product property identifies $F_W$ with $\operatorname{Fix}(c|_W)$. Then
$$
\operatorname{Tr}_{c|_W}(u|_W)=j'^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)\qquad\text{in }\operatorname{Hom}_{D(F_W,A)}(A_{F_W},\omega_{F_W,A}),
$$
where $\operatorname{Tr}$ is the Verdier trace class of [def-trf-trace-class] and, for a section $\sigma:A_F\to\omega_{F,A}$, $j'^*\sigma$ is the composite $A_{F_W}\simeq Lj'^*A_F\xrightarrow{Lj'^*\sigma}Lj'^*\omega_{F,A}\cong Rj'^!\omega_{F,A}\cong\omega_{F_W,A}$ built exactly as the restricted section of [def-trf-local-term] (open-immersion purity and [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition]). When $F_W$ is open and closed in $F$, this is the restricted section $j_{F_W}^*\operatorname{Tr}_c(u)$ of [def-trf-local-term].

source.place: §1.1.9 (restriction u|_W of a c-morphism to an open W of C), §1.2.2(a)-(b) (Tr is a morphism of complexes on C and Tr_beta is its restriction), and the first paragraph of the proof of Theorem 2.1.3 (Fix(c|_W)=Fix(c) on W; replacing C by C \ [Fix(c) \ beta] gives Tr_beta=Tr_c), with the two legs interchanged
